title: Why Memory Ignores Duration and Keeps Only Two Moments
alt_title_1: Fredrickson & Kahneman's Peak-End Rule for Smart Spending
alt_title_2: Stop Buying Longer Vacations (Design for Peak & End Instead)
description_hook: In 1993, psychologists Barbara Fredrickson and Daniel Kahneman proved that human memory largely ignores how long an experience lasts, judging it instead by its emotional peak and final moment. Here is how to apply the Peak-End Rule to spending and work.

scenes.headline: Why a 14-Day Trip Leaves a 4-Day Memory
scenes.stat_label: SNAPSHOTS KEPT BY YOUR REMEMBERING SELF
bullets: Doubling trip length doubles airfare, hotel, and dining bills
Six months later, extra ordinary days blur together
scenes.narration: A fourteen-day luxury vacation costs more than double a five-day trip, yet six months later your memory barely tells them apart.
scenes.source: Fredrickson & Kahneman, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (1993)

scenes.headline: Fredrickson & Kahneman's 1993 Discovery
bullets: Subjects rated episodes of varying length almost identically
Scores tracked the average of Peak intensity and the End
scenes.narration: In 1993, psychologists Barbara Fredrickson and Daniel Kahneman demonstrated duration neglect in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Human memory judges past experiences almost entirely by their emotional peak and final moment.
scenes.source: Barbara L. Fredrickson & Daniel Kahneman, JPSP, Vol. 65, No. 1 (1993)

scenes.headline: Overpaying for Length & Neglecting Handoffs
scenes.left_body: 14 average resort days or sloppy project handoff -> weak recall
scenes.right_body: 4 days with 1 unforgettable peak + seamless final impression
scenes.narration: People overpay for extra mediocre days on trips and let client projects trail off with messy handoffs that sour months of solid craft.

scenes.headline: Fund One Vivid Peak and a Crisp Finish
scenes.stat_label: SHORTER TRIPS + VIVID PEAKS = HIGHER MARGIN
scenes.stat_subtext: Save 50% on duration -> invest in memorable peaks & compounding
scenes.narration: Design for the remembering self: shorten trip length while funding one unforgettable peak day, and close every client deliverable with a crisp, generous finish.

scenes.headline: Invest in Highlights, Bank the Difference
scenes.stat_label: CRAFT THE PEAK • POLISH THE FINAL MINUTE
bullets: Trim forgettable middle days and invest the cash saved
Leave every client and guest with an effortless final step
scenes.narration: Stop paying extra for bland duration; invest your money and craft where peak moments and clean endings live forever.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin application of Fredrickson & Kahneman (1993)
